inputs.userGoal: Create Bicep infrastructure across two subscriptions in the same tenant: one subscription simulates an on-premises environment and the other hosts the Azure migration target, with parameterized VM sizes, one Windows source, and one Linux source.
subGoals: Cost-optimized educational lab with parameterized VM sizes and automatic shutdown schedules.
Security-focused segmentation with private source workloads and CIDR-restricted appliance administration.
Supported automation boundary: infrastructure and the documented Azure Migrate project resource are IaC; generated installers, keys, registration, replication, and migration remain manual.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a source-subscription lifecycle boundary for all simulated on-premises resources.
reasoning.tradeoffs: One resource group is simpler to deploy and clean up but provides less granular RBAC.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates appliances from private simulated physical servers while keeping required discovery and replication paths local.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Subnet segmentation adds NSG rules but avoids peering cost and routing complexity.

properties.inbound: Administrator CIDR to TCP 3389 and discovery UI TCP 44368; workload subnet to replication appliance TCP 443 and 9443
properties.outbound: HTTPS to documented Azure Migrate and Site Recovery endpoints

reasoning.whyChosen: Restricts appliance administration and permits only documented discovery/replication flows.
reasoning.tradeoffs: CIDR-restricted public administration is less isolated than Bastion but materially cheaper for a short-lived lab.

properties.inbound: Discovery appliance to Windows TCP 5985/5986 and Linux TCP 22; replication appliance push-install rules only when documented and enabled

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps source workloads private while allowing discovery and agent onboarding from dedicated appliances.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Windows defaults to documented private-network WinRM HTTP fallback unless the operator supplies a valid HTTPS certificate.

reasoning.whyChosen: Enables low-cost RDP and appliance configuration UI access without exposing source workloads.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public appliance IP is an explicit lab-only security exception.

reasoning.whyChosen: Enables administration of the separate simplified replication appliance.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public appliance IP is an explicit lab-only security exception.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides explicit outbound connectivity for private source workload bootstrap and documented Mobility Service endpoints.
reasoning.tradeoffs: NAT Gateway adds fixed hourly cost but preserves private workload NICs and deterministic egress.

reasoning.whyChosen: Supplies explicit outbound-only connectivity to the private workload subnet.
reasoning.tradeoffs: One shared egress IP reduces attack surface but requires NAT Gateway.

properties.minimum: 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, approximately 80 GB disk

reasoning.whyChosen: Meets the physical discovery appliance requirement and remains separate from replication and workloads.
reasoning.tradeoffs: This VM dominates compute cost but cannot be reduced below the documented appliance floor.

reasoning.whyChosen: Meets the modernized replication appliance CPU/RAM requirement and provides a dedicated cache disk above the 620 GB minimum.
reasoning.tradeoffs: F-series minimizes memory cost; the large cache disk remains mandatory.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a low-cost Windows source with a separate data disk for discovery, inventory, performance collection, and migration experiments.
reasoning.tradeoffs: B-series credits can affect performance observations; the VM size is parameterized for controlled experiments.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a low-cost Linux source on a currently supported Mobility Service distribution with a separate data disk.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The image uses the latest Marketplace build; its kernel must be rechecked against the current Mobility Service support list before replication.

reasoning.whyChosen: Reduces idle lab cost and is parameterized so collection and replication windows can keep machines running.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Schedules must be disabled or moved during continuous performance collection and replication.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a target-subscription lifecycle boundary for Azure Migrate metadata and migrated workloads.
alternativesConsidered: Separate project and workload resource groups
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single target resource group simplifies a lab but production migrations usually separate platform and workload ownership.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides nonoverlapping, isolated test and final migration destinations in the selected target region.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Subnets are simpler and share a VNet boundary; NSGs enforce isolation appropriate for this lab.

properties.inbound: Denied by default; add temporary validation access only through an approved management path

reasoning.whyChosen: Prevents a test-migrated VM from conflicting with or reaching the simulated source environment.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Interactive validation requires a temporary public IP, existing private management path, or Azure Run Command.

properties.inbound: Denied by default; application and management rules are added only during cutover validation

reasoning.whyChosen: Creates a distinct final migration landing subnet with a deny-by-default posture.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Separate subnet adds one NSG but makes test cleanup and final cutover easier to reason about.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides the optional target NAT Gateway with a Standard static outbound address.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Not deployed until target internet egress is explicitly enabled.

reasoning.whyChosen: Optionally provides explicit outbound access to migrated VMs during validation.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Disabled by default to avoid fixed hourly cost until test migration requires it.

reasoning.whyChosen: Uses the official Azure quickstart resource contract to create the Azure Migrate hub project and its server assessment, discovery, and migration solutions in a supported United States metadata location.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public endpoint connectivity avoids Private Link cost and complexity. Portal-generated keys, migration resources, and simplified appliance registration remain manual.

overallReasoning.summary: A subscription-scoped orchestration deployment targets two subscription modules. The source subscription contains isolated appliance and workload subnets. The target subscription contains separate test and final migration subnets. The source and target networks are not peered.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Direct Azure Marketplace VMs minimize cost but Azure Site Recovery documents that failover of Azure VMs treated as physical machines with Marketplace image disks is unsupported. Discovery and assessment are expected; replication, test migration, and final migration are explicitly best-effort. Bastion, zones, backup, Defender for Servers, Log Analytics, flow logs, and target NAT are omitted or optional to limit recurring lab cost. Appliance public IPs are an accepted exception and are restricted to the required administrator CIDR.

plan.validation: Validate with Bicep compilation, lint diagnostics, subscription-scope what-if for both subscriptions, westus3 SKU/quota checks, and manual Azure Migrate prerequisite checks before deployment.
architecturePrinciples: Use explicit and least-privilege network flows
Do not automate undocumented Azure Migrate operations
